line.game.borin.i-need-both-things-in-my.label: I need both things in my satchel first.

line.game.borin.a-pinch-of-dreamcap-a-sp.label: A pinch of dreamcap, a splash of stout. Sweet dreams, large unpleasant fellow.

line.game.borin.an-inspired-idea-unfortu.label: An inspired idea. Unfortunately, inspiration is not enough here.

line.game.borin.a-discreet-splash-now-to.label: A discreet splash. Now to wait for his next drink.

line.game.borin.the-knots-are-secure-if-.label: The knots are secure. If the noise wakes you, Grub, you will have to complain from there.

line.game.borin.that-is-no-longer-in-my-.label: That is no longer in my satchel.

line.game.borin.he-is-watching-wait-unti.label: He is watching! Wait until he turns his back, then try the brew again.

line.game.borin.he-would-never-let-me-ti.label: He would never let me tie him up while he is awake. Sleep first, knots second.

line.game.borin.one-clang-and-that-guard.label: One clang and that guard will catch us. Quiet first, heroics second.

line.game.borin.breaking-the-lock-might-.label: Breaking the lock might wake him. I should tie up Grub first.

line.game.borin.i-cannot-see-how-that-wo.label: I cannot see how that would help here.

line.game.borin.one-copper-coin-enough-t.label: One copper coin. Enough to buy an idea a drink.

line.game.borin.never-go-on-a-rescue-wit.label: Never go on a rescue without a rope. Father was quite firm about that.

line.game.borin.i-should-ask-someone-abo.label: I should ask someone about these before I put them in my bag. Or my mouth.

line.game.borin.a-dreamcap-mara-said-it-.label: A dreamcap. Mara said it makes a very effective sleeping draught when mixed with stout.

line.game.borin.the-tool-chest-is-empty-.label: The tool chest is empty. Its pickaxe is in capable, if rather small, hands.

line.game.borin.orrins-finest-pickaxe-fo.label: Orrin’s finest pickaxe. For the king.

line.game.borin.sound-asleep-and-securel.label: Sound asleep and securely tied. Those knots should hold him while we escape.

line.game.borin.sound-asleep-but-breakin.label: Sound asleep, but breaking that lock could wake him. Better tie him up first.

line.game.borin.start-at-home-a-copper-c.label: Start at home. A copper coin and a strong rope may come in handy.

line.game.borin.visit-the-pub-ask-mara-a.label: Visit the pub. Ask Mara about the orcs and Orrin about the mine.

line.game.borin.select-the-copper-coin-i.label: Select the copper coin in your satchel, then give it to Mara.

line.game.borin.mara-described-the-silve.label: Mara described the silver-spotted mushrooms beside the forest path.

line.game.borin.select-the-dreamcap-then.label: Select the dreamcap, then select the stout to combine them.

line.game.borin.search-the-open-chest-fo.label: Search the open chest for Orrin’s pickaxe.

line.game.borin.the-runed-chest-in-goldr.label: The runed chest in Goldroot Mine opens with Orrin’s words.

line.game.borin.the-stew-is-ready-let-gr.label: The stew is ready. Let Grub finish his next drink.

line.game.borin.at-the-camp-use-the-drea.label: At the camp, use the dreamcap stout on the cauldron when the guard turns away.

line.game.borin.use-the-climbing-rope-on.label: Use the climbing rope on the sleeping Grub before the noise of breaking the lock wakes him.

line.game.borin.use-the-pickaxe-on-the-c.label: Use the pickaxe on the cage’s lock. The way home is almost open.

line.game.borin.the-king-is-home-there-a.label: The king is home. There are worse reasons to have another round.

line.game.borin.the-stew-is-ready-i-shou.label: The stew is ready. I should keep hidden until he falls asleep.

line.game.borin.i-need-to-keep-hidden-a-.label: I need to keep hidden. A little sleeping draught in that cauldron could give me a chance.

line.game.borin.i-cannot-reach-that-from.label: I cannot reach that from here. There needs to be a walkable path.

line.game.borin.that-route-is-blocked-ba.label: That route is blocked. Back to cover.

The body is at its lowest point of the contact phase. Both feet are flat or planted on the ground.Frame 3 (Passing): The passing position. The right leg swings past the stationary left leg, knees pass each other, and the body rises back to neutral height.Frame 4 (Up / High Point): The body reaches its highest vertical point as the character pushes off the back foot, with the passing leg extending forward.Frame 5 (Contact - Right Foot Forward): Mirror of Frame 1. The right heel makes contact ahead, and the left toe prepares to lift. Legs are at maximum width again.Frame 6 (Down / Recoil): Mirror of Frame 2. The body dips as weight shifts onto the right leg, with the right knee bending to cushion the impact.Frame 7 (Passing): Mirror of Frame 3. The left leg swings past the right leg moving forward, and the body rises back up.Frame 8 (Up / High Point): Mirror of Frame 4. The body reaches its peak height on the right foot before transitioning smoothly back into Frame 1.
